learn.title: One understandable batch
learn.body: Ask for a change that delivers one coherent part of the specification. A small batch has fewer interactions to inspect and is easier to explain, test and undo. Small is not a fixed line count: the batch must fit its risks and the review attention actually available.

learn.title: Keep a way back
learn.body: Before AI edits, establish a Git checkpoint, often a commit of the intended current work. It preserves a known state to inspect or return to if the new approach fails. A checkpoint is not proof that the state works, so record the checks that support it and avoid overwriting unrelated work.

learn.title: Match size to risk
learn.body: A wording change with a clear check may fit in a larger batch than a change to stored completions, login or permissions. Increase scrutiny when a mistake could lose data or expose information. Split work when you cannot comfortably explain its files, behavior and tradeoffs in one review.

learn.title: Read the actual difference
learn.body: A diff shows additions, removals and modifications rather than a summary of intent. Compare it with the request and acceptance criteria. Check every changed file, question unrelated renames or formatting, and inspect surrounding code when context matters. AI's summary is a guide, not a substitute for the diff.

learn.title: Review one habit tracker change
learn.body: The agreed slice adds check-off behavior without redesigning the habit tracker.
steps: Record the current checks and make a Git checkpoint before requesting edits.
Request only same-day habit completion, leaving reminders and visual redesign out of scope.
Open the diff and map each changed file to storage, the completion control or its check.
Notice an unrelated rename of existing habit fields; remove it rather than accepting extra migration risk.
Check the final behavior and diff, explain why each edit belongs, then commit only the accepted change.

learn.body: Do not accept a diff you cannot explain. Ask for a walkthrough, split the work or discard the attempt. AI can propose code; the human retains understanding and ownership.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a Git checkpoint before AI edits?
choices: Preserve a known state that can be inspected or restored
Prove that every current feature works correctly
Make all later generated edits safe automatically
questions.explanation: A checkpoint gives you a reference and a way back. It does not verify the saved state or make later changes correct.

questions.prompt: A \_\_ shows the additions, removals and modifications made to files.
questions.explanation: A diff exposes the actual edits. Reviewing it helps you find unexpected files and unrelated changes that a short summary might omit.

questions.prompt: Match each proposed batch to the most suitable response.
pairs: Fix one label with a clear check
A small batch is likely reviewable
Change completion storage and add accounts
Pause, reduce scope or request a walkthrough
questions.explanation: Batch size depends on coupling, risk and your capacity to review. Unrelated outcomes and unexplained edits need clearer boundaries, not blind acceptance.

questions.prompt: Put a reviewable AI-assisted change in order.
steps: Inspect the complete diff and relevant context
Check behavior against the acceptance criteria
Accept and commit only edits you understand
questions.explanation: A checkpoint protects the starting point. Review and behavioral checks come before accepting the new state; a generated summary cannot replace either.

questions.prompt: What three-letter word names the file-by-file comparison you inspect before accepting generated edits?
questions.explanation: The diff is the concrete record of what changed. Inspecting it supports deliberate acceptance instead of trusting a description of the work.

questions.prompt: AI adds habit check-off behavior and also rewrites unrelated storage code. Tests for check-off pass. What is the best response?
choices: Review the rewrite separately and remove or defer it if it is unnecessary
Accept everything because one passing check covers all changed code
Keep the rewrite hidden so the diff stays short
Add another unrelated feature to make the batch worthwhile
questions.explanation: The extra rewrite expands risk beyond the agreed outcome. A passing check-off test does not establish the safety of unrelated storage changes.
